label: copy step L+1 when the first original token is "s" (fed back as input), long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase at step t = L+1 (recall_idx 1, i.e. the step right after <DEL>), when the input there is the model fed-back first output "s" (first original token = s). Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, at any other copy position, or for other first tokens (in_tok s accounts for ~100% of mass; a handful of tiny activations on v/w/u). Requires L >= 6: zero activity for L = 3..5; at L = 6 it fires weakly and only on about half the eligible sequences (most false positives are L=6), while at L >= 7 it fires on essentially every eligible sequence (precision 1.0 for L>=7). Magnitude grows with sequence length (top activations ~4.1 are all L = 9; L = 6 examples are ~0.05-0.3 of max). Insensitive to the identity of the token being output, digits count, or repeats.

issues: The test scores reproduce: P 0.895, R 0.996, F1 0.943, mass recall 0.9999. On the dev split, all activation mass falls in the copy phase at recall_idx 1, with in_tok s holding 100% of it. Nothing fires for L = 3..5.
L = 6 on its own scores P 0.57, R 0.16, mass recall 0.023. L >= 7 scores P 1.0, R 0.84. Both match the claims, and L >= 6 gives the better F1.

Minor overclaim: the explanation says firing does not depend on digits or repeats, but at L = 6 it does somewhat. Precision is 0.37 when in_count >= 2 versus 0.62 when in_count == 1, and 0.73 when n_digits >= 2 versus 0.50 when n_digits == 0. This looks like graded modulation near the firing threshold, not a clean rule, and L = 6 carries only about 2% of the mass.

The 37 missed activations on the test split are near-zero (0.00-0.02 of max) and carry 0% of the mass. All are at step 10 (L = 9) with first token v, w or u, and most have '2' as the third token. This is negligible.
